verdicts.claim: 01.08 Trader vs Private Seller Classification specifies its entire normative content against EU/UK consumer law, which meta/constraints.md's ratified US-first jurisdiction parameterization forbids as an implicit default — leaving the launch market's trader rules unspecified for a fail-closed listing precondition.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED on three independent grounds. (a) The EU/UK material is legal background, not normative platform content: the Overview sentence is prefixed "Under EU/UK consumer law" (01.08-trader-status-classification.md:10) and 01.08:29 explicitly disowns the mechanics the claim says are missing — "It does **not** own: consumer rights mechanics (returns, withdrawal windows, warranties), which belong to 13/14/05, or tax/VAT treatment". The VAT field is hedged: "(where applicable) a company or VAT number" (:25). The Fan-facing disclosure copy is jurisdiction-neutral ("this seller is a private individual; consumer protections do not apply", :19). (b) The jurisdictional variance is a LIVE tracked deferral with owner and target: 01.08 Q-01:92 ("[OWNER]" detection/disposition, User → /create-prd) and Q-02:93 ("Does the classification vary by jurisdiction? Thresholds and duties differ", User → /create-prd-security), and both edge-case rows route to it (:43 "The concrete numeric threshold is jurisdiction-specific and deferred to /create-prd-security (Q-02)"; :46 "See Q-02"). (c) The cited constraint does not reach this file: meta/constraints.md:349 scopes the jurisdiction-profile rule to "the statutory-record vocabulary that domain 16 and its consumers depend on", and 01.02.01 Q-03:163 states affirmatively that the buyer-jurisdiction consumer-law floor "does not resolve against the place-record regime profile D-14 uses". An implementer can build the whole file: three-value classification (:25), situational declaration flow (D-03:84), fail-closed gate (D-04:85, :48, :58, :59), blocking pre-listing disclosure (D-05:86).

verdicts.claim: The domain CX file requires an owner-less org to keep accepting bookings and states it is explicitly not frozen, while 01.03.01 states the same org is frozen and 01.03.03's fail-closed mandate rule makes acceptance impossible.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD but overstated. All quotes verbatim: identity-profiles-organizations-cx.md:305 "Critically the org is **not** frozen"; :314 "the org must still accept it; who settles it waits on succession"; 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:114 "Read paths continue working — the org is frozen, not broken"; 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md D-05:112 "Resolution fails closed"; `book` is in the seven-activity enum (01.03.03 D-01:108); 01.02.02:163 "It is **not** frozen". The word-level contradiction is real and unmarked, and no file names an actor who can accept a new booking while zero confirmed full-mandate holders exist — 01.03.01:114 says outright "no one can act for this org". Downgraded to warning because an implementer is not blocked: three of the four sources converge on "existing obligations continue, settlement deferred" (01.02.02:163-164 "Org keeps trading via succession"; 01.10-estates-legacy-accounts.md:18 "a venue whose sole owner dies still has shows booked next week"; cx:311 "the org keeps operating unadministrable"), and the residual authority hole is carried by two LIVE [OWNER] questions targeting /create-prd — 01.03.01 Q-04:187 ("for single-member and non-band orgs, the selection rule is still live") and 01.10 Q-01:99 ("who can administer a catalogue that keeps earning", with 01.10:47 marked "[PENDING — Q-01 owner decision, /create-prd]"). What survives is the unreconciled "frozen"/"not frozen" wording and the missing accept-vs-queue rule, not an unbuildable spec.

verdicts.claim: Two files in this unit specify behaviour for co-owned 'shared' aliases — a switcher context source, a co-owner notification fan-out, and a concurrency presence indicator — after 01.01.02 D-04 ratified that aliases are single-owner by construction.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD but overstated. Quotes verbatim: 01.01.02-artist-names-aliases-projects.md D-04:152 "A shared name is a band org (01.02.01 type `band`), not a co-owned alias. Aliases are single-owner by construction"; Q-01:165 "RESOLVED — D-04 ... (Number retained: sub-domain CX-02 and the sub-domain index Q-02 both reference 'Q-01 on 01.01.02')"; 01.01-person-identity-roles-cx.md:54, :55 ("a shared alias fans out to all co-owners"), :56; 01.01.03-acting-context-switcher.md:34 ("including shared aliases, subject to 01.01.02 Q-01") and :123. The stale text is real, and cx:55's fan-out sentence is unhedged. Downgraded to warning because the ownership model is stated unambiguously in the owning file — 01.01.02:32 "An alias is a **named professional identity owned by exactly one person record** (D-04 — co-ownership is a band, not an alias)" — and every stale site carries an explicit one-hop pointer to 01.01.02 Q-01, whose target reads RESOLVED. 01.01.03:123 even self-limits ("this file does not resolve the ontology, only its switcher consequence"), and once the ontology resolves to `band` the row collapses into the row immediately above it (:122, the band shared-inbox case) which already prescribes the same presence indicator — so the two readings converge on one build. This is stale-reference hygiene against a ratified decision, not a forced invention of the alias ownership model.

verdicts.claim: Two cross-cut gaps in the domain CX file are deferred only to /ideate-validate, a stage that completed 2026-07-18, and are covered by no live tracked question.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD. Quotes verbatim: identity-profiles-organizations-cx.md:187 (CX-08 §5) "A private seller reclassified to trader with live listings — do their existing listings retroactively publish their address? Unmodelled and consequential. `[PENDING — /ideate-validate]`"; :325 (CX-17 §5) routes the same race to CX-08 §5 with the same dead marker; :77 (CX-02 §5) "the merge-vs-claim ordering for person records remains for validation. `[PENDING — /ideate-validate]`". The target stage is closed: ideation-index.md:148 and :163 both head sections "(`/ideate-validate`, 2026-07-18)", and D-28:214 records "Constraints locked (`/ideate-validate`)". The file itself is dated 2026-07-23 (cx:6) and claims "Step-5 pendings resolved where downstream evidence now exists" (cx:5), so these survived a reconciliation pass. The tracking is malformed rather than merely stale: no owner, and a target stage that cannot run again — which the tree elsewhere treats as a defect requiring re-targeting (01.02.02 Q-01:264 and Q-02:265 both "Re-targeted 2026-07-23: /ideate-validate has already run without taking it"; 01.07 Q-04:109 "This is a **live** deferral, not an expired one"). verdicts.claim: This unit's CX file states an attribute-union rule its own child explicitly labels as corrected, and declares 'unmodelled' a gap its other child announces resolving — and the child records that the parent was knowingly left unedited.

Corrections verbatim: 01.02.01-organization-types-attributes.md:41 "Union collisions are only possible on `party` scope ... | DT-04; corrects parent CX-01 Q1" and :74 "Two types declare the same attribute name with different meanings (studio hourly rate vs venue hire fee ...) | **No collision. Warning is the correct grade rather than blocking: the correction is one hop away in the file that owns the attribute declaration contract (01.02.01:35-45), and both halves of the divergence are explicitly back-cited from the child, so a diligent implementer converges.

verdicts.claim: 01.02.01 specifies the `floored` returns-policy rule as shipped behaviour — a write rejection plus copy asserting a 14-day cancellation right — for a launch market constraints.md says has no such right.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The quote at 01.02.01-organization-types-attributes.md:82 is verbatim, but the mechanism it specifies is already jurisdiction-parameterized in the same sentence: "the statutory floor **for the buyer's jurisdiction** is rendered as non-editable platform text" — not an EU floor asserted as universal. The '14-day' string sits in the "User Sees" column, i.e. illustrative UI copy generated from whatever floor resolves; the tree explicitly labels this class of figure as illustration elsewhere (01.03.03 D-08:115 "the GBP figures in this file and in 01.04.01 are narrative illustration and **must not** be read as defaults"). Decisively, the open floor is a LIVE tracked deferral in the same file: Q-03:163 "**Still open for `floored` authority (DT-10)**: the statutory returns floor is a property of the *buyer's* jurisdiction, not the record's address, so it does not resolve against the place-record regime profile D-14 uses, and no source states which floors apply" — owner User, target `/create-prd-security`, with 13/14. Q-03 therefore both tracks the gap and rebuts the claim's premise that D-14/constraints.md D-72 governs this field. Two implementers converge: build a `floored` field bounded by the buyer-jurisdiction floor, which resolves to no bound where no floor exists (D-14:155's own rule).

verdicts.claim: The same trigger — an org's sole owning-mandate holder dying, being suspended, or deleting their account — produces two differently-named states with two different succession mechanisms in two sibling files, each claiming to close the same cross-cut gap.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. Quotes are verbatim but the two names are explicitly bridged, not competing: 01.03.03 D-04:111 "Every org must retain at least one full mandate holder | Enforced at departure (01.03.01) and creation (01.02.02); **an ownerless org is unadministrable**", and identity-profiles-organizations-cx.md:311 uses both in one clause ("the org keeps operating unadministrable") while :305 sources the `ownerless` enum to 01.02 D-16. So `ownerless` is the ownership-axis state (01.02.02:84) and `unadministrable` is the administrative condition it produces (01.03.01:114) — one model, two layers. The two 'mechanisms' likewise compose rather than conflict: D-16:257 supplies only "`ownerless` + a succession route" without mechanics, and 01.03.01 D-14:173 supplies the mechanics while explicitly narrowing its own scope to "(a) single-member orgs, (b) every non-band org type ... (c) the **uncapped** owning mandate". Where no member remains the estate route (01.10) is the only one available; where members remain, an owner-transfer offer is exactly what 01.02.02:163's pointer to 01.05.03 ("contested claims & ownership transfer") names. The claim's premise that both files claim the same gap is also wrong: D-16:257 makes no gap claim. And the residual — which selection rule fires for these populations — is a LIVE [OWNER] deferral at 01.03.01 Q-04:187 ("For the uncapped owning mandate, and for single-member and non-band orgs, the selection rule is still live and still a product decision", User → /create-prd).

verdicts.claim: 01.04.02 carries a live edge case for a band that is 'a shared alias rather than an org', concluding name ownership then has no governance home — a scenario 01.01.02 D-04 made unreachable.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED. The quote at 01.04.02-name-trademark-ownership.md:48 is verbatim, and the row is indeed stale relative to 01.01.02 D-04:152. But it forces nothing and instructs no build: its antecedent is an explicit conditional on the very question that resolved ("Band is a shared alias rather than an org (**01.01.02 Q-01**)"), its consequent is purely negative ("has no governance home"), and it is flagged "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — real evidence for 01.01.02 Q-01" in a file whose status is `[SURFACE]` (:5, dated 2026-07-16, pre-ratification). Following the row's own pointer reaches 01.01.02 Q-01:165 "**RESOLVED — D-04**: it is a band org", which makes the condition false and the row vacuous. The post-ratification consequence is already recorded in the correct direction at identity-profiles-organizations-cx.md:237 (CX-12) "Because D-04 makes a shared name a band, 01.04's governance capture must be reachable **from** alias creation". No implementer builds a governance-less shared-name path from a vacuous negative row that cites a resolved question. Stale-marker hygiene, not ambiguity.

verdicts.claim: A shadow party's name may be up to 120 characters and D-13 requires that name to become an alias on claim, but an alias display name is capped at 100 characters — a 20-character band in which a legal shadow name cannot become the alias it is specified to become.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD. All four quotes verbatim: 01.05.01-shadow-party-creation-invitation.md:43 "| **Name** | Yes | 1–120 characters, counted and compared after the name is normalized"; D-09:210 "a name (≤120 chars, no URLs, no markup)"; D-13:214 "A shadow party's name is alias-shaped, not person-shaped. **Claiming binds it as an alias of a person**"; :53 "on claim it becomes an alias of a person (01.01.02)". Contradicted by 01.01.02-artist-names-aliases-projects.md:36 "| **Display name** | 1–100 characters, full Unicode". A repo-wide grep of the domain for these limits returns exactly these three sites and nothing that reconciles them — neither file references the other's number, and no open question in 01.05.01 or 01.01.02 raises it. Two constraints in the vision layer, both stated as normative, that cannot both hold at the domain's named conversion event (D-13). Kept at warning, not raised: the affected input range (101–120 characters) is vanishingly rare for a real artist name, so the consequence is bounded even though the resolution (truncate / reject the claim / widen the alias cap) is a genuine product choice.

verdicts.claim: 01.06.03 ratifies the per-recipient EPK link as 'a tracking wrapper over public content, not an access gate' while the same file says the EPK may carry rates and contact routes 'not meant for the world', leaving the confidentiality status of EPK content undetermined.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — a live tracked deferral covers exactly this, and the finding's own quote truncates the pointer to it. 01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md:52 reads in full "| Link is shared publicly | An EPK **may contain rates and contact routes not meant for the world** | Needs expiry/revocation. **See Q-02**" — the finding's evidence stops before the route. Q-03:105 then tracks it explicitly: "Do share links expire or get revoked, given an EPK may carry rates and contact routes?" — owner Agent, target `/create-prd-security`. Q-02:104 separately confirms the model is not in question ("D-01 fixes the EPK as a generated view and D-06 makes the per-recipient link 'a tracking wrapper over public content, not an access gate' ... What is open is purely whether to also ship the export"), mirrored at the parent index Q-02:58. D-06:97's scope is stated in its own context column — "Forwarding to a decision-making room must work for strangers with no account (D-03)" — i.e. no login wall, which is orthogonal to link expiry, and :54 already forbids the one genuinely sensitive class ("No path from the EPK to the legal identity surface (01.01.04 D-01) | Never rendered"). The finding itself concedes the convergent reading; an unguessable, expiring, revocable, non-account-gated link satisfies every cited statement.
